title: General best practices for endpoints
provenance: Original statements written for MoonMind. Each requirement names rules of the ComplianceAsCode (SCAP Security Guide) standard profile, xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_standard, by their XCCDF identifiers only; no benchmark or ComplianceAsCode text is reproduced.
attribution: MoonMind general best practices for endpoints: original statements by the MoonMind maintainers, Apache-2.0. Rule identifiers refer to ComplianceAsCode content, used under its own identity and BSD-3-Clause license.
conclusions: Per-requirement conclusions from OpenSCAP evaluation of the ComplianceAsCode standard profile, xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_standard. A requirement is satisfied only when every named rule passed in a complete, current result for the endpoint. An offline copy or imported result is not MoonMind's own observation of the running device.
limitations: Offline copies decide only file-content rules; ownership, permission and runtime rules need OpenSCAP results produced on the endpoint.
Linux distributions with shipped ComplianceAsCode content only; Windows, macOS, mobile devices and regulated gaming devices are unsupported.
Qualification against real fleet devices is Unverified until an operator compares device results with the fixture qualification.

requirements.title: Remote root login is refused
requirements.summary: The SSH server refuses direct logins as root, so administration happens through named accounts.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply a root filesystem or image archive of the endpoint, or OpenSCAP results produced on it, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: The listed rules decide this on an offline root filesystem or image copy and on imported device results alike.

objectives.description: The SSH server configuration sets PermitRootLogin no.

requirements.title: Remote logins need a password
requirements.summary: The SSH server refuses accounts with empty passwords.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply a root filesystem or image archive of the endpoint, or OpenSCAP results produced on it, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: The listed rules decide this on an offline root filesystem or image copy and on imported device results alike.

objectives.description: The SSH server configuration sets PermitEmptyPasswords no.

requirements.title: Legacy cleartext services are absent
requirements.summary: Telnet and NIS server packages, which carry credentials in the clear, are not installed.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply a root filesystem or image archive of the endpoint, or OpenSCAP results produced on it, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: The listed rules decide this on an offline root filesystem or image copy and on imported device results alike.

objectives.description: The telnetd and nis packages are not installed.

requirements.title: Security events are recorded
requirements.summary: The audit daemon and the system logger are installed, so security events leave a record.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply a root filesystem or image archive of the endpoint, or OpenSCAP results produced on it, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: The listed rules decide this on an offline root filesystem or image copy and on imported device results alike.

objectives.description: The audit and rsyslog packages are installed.

requirements.title: Account databases are protected
requirements.summary: The password and shadow databases are owned by root with restrictive permissions.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply OpenSCAP results (ARF or XCCDF) produced on the endpoint itself, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: Ownership, permissions and runtime state are not kept in an offline copy; only OpenSCAP results produced on the endpoint decide this, so an offline copy leaves it inconclusive.

objectives.description: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow have the ownership and modes the standard profile requires.

requirements.title: Kernel exploit mitigations are on
requirements.summary: Address space layout randomization is on and set-user-ID programs do not dump core.
requirements.applicability: Every Linux endpoint in the plan whose distribution the shipped ComplianceAsCode content supports.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Supply OpenSCAP results (ARF or XCCDF) produced on the endpoint itself, as an artifact of the saved environment.
requirements.objectiveBasis: Ownership, permissions and runtime state are not kept in an offline copy; only OpenSCAP results produced on the endpoint decide this, so an offline copy leaves it inconclusive.

objectives.description: kernel.randomize_va_space is 2 and fs.suid_dumpable is 0, at runtime and in configuration.
